outcome: type of birth (cesarean section, forceps-assisted birth)
newborn admission to neonatal intensive or intermediate care units
cohort: 3,397 women admitted for childbirth at a Freestanding Birth Centre and their newborns.
finding: Primiparity was a predictor of increased interventions and unfavorable maternal and neonatal outcomes, although the studied Freestanding Birth Centre was considered a safe setting for childbirth among healthy pregnant women.
mod_finding: Primiparity was associated with a higher likelihood of cesarean section and forceps-assisted birth, while overall, births predominantly occurred in semi-seated and upright positions.
cross-section timing: During childbirth and the immediate postpartum period.
